economy.summary: His campaign site proposes tax credits of up to $500,000 for small businesses to help them compete with large corporations, state-funded construction of affordable apartment housing, and expansion of public transportation to underserved communities.
economy.short: Proposes small-business tax credits, affordable housing, expanded public transit.

taxes.summary: His campaign site says he would work to reduce taxes for fixed-income individuals and families living below the poverty line, and to fight unfunded state mandates that burden homeowners.
taxes.short: Proposes reducing taxes on fixed-income, below-poverty households.

abortion.summary: Told WESA's 2026 voter guide that he will advocate for reproductive freedoms; neither the guide nor his campaign site details specific policy proposals.
abortion.short: Says he will advocate for reproductive freedoms; no detail.

education.summary: Told WESA that public schools should not have to be burdened by the high tuition of for-profit cyber schools, and that he opposes unfunded mandates like PSERS that reduce school funding.
education.short: Opposes cyber-school tuition burden and unfunded mandates on schools.

healthcare.summary: His campaign site says he will work with other representatives and experts to develop a proposal to revise healthcare options, with an aim to provide universal healthcare for all.
healthcare.short: Proposes developing plan aiming at universal healthcare for all.

energy.summary: His campaign site says he would work with the Department of Environmental Protection on proper cleanup protocols, support community cleanups, and stop the unhindered expansion of AI data centers, which he says do not provide long-term jobs.
energy.short: Supports environmental cleanups; opposes unhindered AI data center expansion.

abortion.summary: Voted in December 2021 for Senate Bill 106, a package of proposed state constitutional amendments that included a provision stating there is no constitutional right to taxpayer-funded abortion or any other right relating to abortion.
abortion.short: Voted for amendment: no state constitutional right to abortion.

education.summary: Said in a 2021 candidate survey that every parent has the right to choose the best education and way of learning that suits their child, and that schools need to be open.
education.short: Says parents have the right to choose child's education.

healthcare.summary: In a 2021 candidate survey she strongly disagreed with the statement that it is the government's responsibility to ensure everyone has health insurance.
healthcare.short: Strongly disagrees government must ensure everyone has health insurance.

energy.summary: Said in a 2021 candidate survey that she supports anything that can be done to keep Pennsylvania's coal, oil, and gas jobs alive.
energy.short: Supports keeping Pennsylvania coal, oil, and gas jobs alive.

guns.summary: In a 2021 candidate survey she answered yes to allowing teachers to carry guns at school and, asked what gun restrictions are needed to protect public safety, wrote that it is our constitutional right to bear arms.
guns.short: Supports armed teachers; cites constitutional right to bear arms.
